```{r - load data}
# List all .xlsx files in the folder
xlsx_files <- list.files(dir.assignments, pattern = "^A\\d{2}_queue_.*\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE)
xlsx_files
# Read and combine all files with filename as a new column
all_data <- map_dfr(xlsx_files, function(file) {

  df$source_file <- basename(file)  # Add filename as a column

## remove already coded data
all_data_left <- all_data %>%
  mutate(coder = substr(source_file, 1, 3)) %>%

    engagement_coder     = NA_character_,
    engagement_rationale = NA_character_,
    comments_coder       = NA_character_,

  ) %>%
  select(-any_of(c('source_file', 'coder'))) %>%
  ## add `goals_llm`
  left_join(., 
            sampled_df %>% 
              select(statement_id, goals_llm), 
            by = 'statement_id') %>%
  select(1:targets_nlp, goals_llm, everything())
```

```{r - add statements before and after}

filter_company_year <- unique(all_data_left$company_year)




## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## coded data with text and sdgs, including rows without detected sdgs 
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


## 1.1 coded data for 2020, 2022, 2024
csvname <- paste0('coded_combined_all_with_raw_330_tokenize_2020_2022_2024.csv')
f <- paste0(dir.coded.comb, csvname);  f
coded_combined_after2018 <- readr::read_csv(f, show_col_types = F) 


## 1.2. coded data for 2018
csvname <- paste0('coded_combined_all_with_raw_352_tokenize_2018.csv')
f <- paste0(dir.reports, 'pdf_coded_human/DF_coded_comb/', csvname);  f
coded_combined_before2018 <- readr::read_csv(f, show_col_types = F) 


## 1.3 combine all 4 years data
coded_combined_all <- rbind(coded_combined_before2018, coded_combined_after2018) %>%
  group_by(company, year) %>%
  # add a row ID within each group
  mutate(row_id = row_number() ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    company_year  = paste0(company, "_", year),
    statement_oid = paste0(company, "_", year, "_", row_id)
  ) 


## filter the full data to reduce data size 
coded_combined_all_filter <- coded_combined_all %>%
  filter(company_year %in% filter_company_year) %>%
  select(statement_oid, company_year, statement)




## 3. join to the original data to add more sentences

all_data_left_plus <- all_data_left %>%
  mutate(.row_id = row_number()) %>%
  left_join(., 
            coded_combined_all_filter, 
            by = c('statement', 'company_year'))


# Count how many rows each original x row became
duplicates <- all_data_left_plus %>%
  count(.row_id) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

# Inspect the actual duplicated rows if needed
duplicated_rows <- all_data_left_plus %>% 
  filter(.row_id %in% duplicates$.row_id)

## if there are just a few duplicates, we simply keeo the first match 
all_data_left_plus <- all_data_left_plus %>%
  dplyr::distinct(statement_id, .keep_all = T) %>%
  select(-any_of(c('company_year', '.row_id')))

target_oids <- unique(all_data_left_plus$statement_oid)


## 4. subset a data frame based on a list of `statement_oid` and include one row before and one row after each match

# Step 1: Decompose statement_oid into components
# df_with_keys <- all_data_left_plus %>%
#   mutate(
#     company = str_extract(statement_oid, "^[^_]+"),
#     year = str_extract(statement_oid, "(?<=_)[0-9]{4}(?=_)"),
#     row_id = as.integer(str_extract(statement_oid, "[0-9]+$"))
#   )

# Step 2: Parse target_oids into company, year, row_id
target_oids_split <- tibble(statement_oid = target_oids) %>%
  mutate(
    company = str_extract(statement_oid, "^[^_]+"),
    year = str_extract(statement_oid, "(?<=_)[0-9]{4}(?=_)"),
    row_id = as.integer(str_extract(statement_oid, "[0-9]+$")),
    group_id = row_number()
  ) %>%
  ## add "statement_id" back
  left_join(., all_data_left_plus %>% select(statement_id, statement_oid),
            by = 'statement_oid')

# Step 3: Add +/- 1 row_id per target
target_oids_expanded <- target_oids_split %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(neighbor_ids = list(row_id + c(-1, 0, 1))) %>%
  unnest(neighbor_ids) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ## create unique oid for later use
  dplyr::mutate(oid_expanded = paste(company, year, neighbor_ids, sep='_')) %>%
  # dplyr::rename('statement_oid_llm' = 'statement_oid') %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Step 3. To combine each set of three neighbor rows into one single string from the "statement" column
coded_text_expanded <- target_oids_expanded %>% 
  select(group_id, statement_id, statement_oid, oid_expanded) %>%
  ## link to the statement text 
  left_join(., coded_combined_all_filter, 
             by = c('oid_expanded' = 'statement_oid')) %>%
  group_by(group_id, statement_id, statement_oid) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(statement_expanded = paste(statement, collapse = " "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  select(-group_id)


# Step 4: add the `statement_expanded` to the assignment data
all_data_left_plus_expanded <- all_data_left_plus %>%
  select(-statement_oid) %>%
  left_join(., coded_text_expanded, 
            by = 'statement_id') %>%
  select(1:statement, statement_expanded, everything())
```



```{r - assign}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)


all_data_left_bygoal <- all_data_left_plus_expanded %>%
  ## split a column with comma-separated SDGs and convert the data frame to long format
  separate_rows(goals_llm, sep = ",") %>%         # Split by comma
  mutate(goals_llm = trimws(goals_llm))           # Remove any leading/trailing whitespace



# Coder preferences: list of SDG goals per coder -------------------------------
# Use the SAME format you keep in goals_llm after normalization (see normalizer below).
# Below are examples; replace with your team’s real preferences.
coder_sdgs <- list(
  B1 = c(1, 6, 13, 14),
  B2 = c(5, 6, 9, 10, 14, 16),
  B3 = c(1, 3, 4, 5, 10, 17),
  B4 = c(2, 7, 8, 12, 15),
  B5 = c(2, 7, 11, 13, 15, 17),
  B6 = c(3, 4, 8, 9, 11, 16, 12)
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# INPUTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# df: your statements, one row per statement
# must contain:
#   - statement_id
#   - statement_text
#   - goals_llm (semicolon-separated, e.g., "SDG07; SDG13" or "7;13" is fine)
# Optional:
#   - any other columns you want to carry through




# ----------------------------
# Inputs & guards
# ----------------------------
stopifnot(all(c("statement_id", "statement", "goals_llm") %in% names(all_data_left_bygoal)))

annotators <- names(coder_sdgs)  # e.g., c("B1","B2","B3","B4","B5","B6")
stopifnot(length(annotators) >= 2)




# ----------------------------
# Helpers
# ----------------------------

# parse goals_llm to integer SDG codes (1..17)
parse_goals_to_int <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || x == "") return(integer(0))
  toks <- unlist(strsplit(x, ";"))
  toks <- str_trim(toks)
  # extract digits (handles "SDG7", "sdg07", "7")
  nums <- as.integer(stringr::str_extract(toks, "\\d+"))
  nums <- nums[!is.na(nums)]
  nums <- nums[nums >= 1 & nums <= 17]
  unique(nums)
}

# overlap score between statement SDGs and coder's preference
overlap_score <- function(stmt_sdgs, coder_pref) {
  if (length(stmt_sdgs) == 0 || length(coder_pref) == 0) return(0L)
  sum(stmt_sdgs %in% coder_pref)
}

# choose best coder given overlap then current load; optionally exclude one coder
pick_best_coder <- function(candidates, stmt_sdgs, loads, prefs_list, exclude = character(0)) {
  cands <- setdiff(candidates, exclude)
  if (length(cands) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  sc <- vapply(cands, function(cdr) overlap_score(stmt_sdgs, prefs_list[[cdr]] %||% integer(0)),
               FUN.VALUE = integer(1))
  tibble(coder_id = cands, score = sc, load = loads[cands]) %>%
    arrange(desc(score), load, coder_id) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    pull(coder_id)
}

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x




# ----------------------------
# Prepare per-statement SDG set
# ----------------------------
stmts <- all_data_left_bygoal %>%
  mutate(sdg_set = lapply(goals_llm, parse_goals_to_int))

# If stratum missing, create a single stratum
if (!"stratum" %in% names(stmts)) {
  stmts <- stmts %>% mutate(stratum = "_ALL_")
}


# ----------------------------
# Preference-aware, balanced double assignment
# ----------------------------
assign_pref_double <- function(df_group, coder_prefs) {
  N <- nrow(df_group)
  if (N == 0) return(df_group %>% mutate(coder_1 = NA_character_, coder_2 = NA_character_))

  # initialize loads at 0 for all annotators
  loads <- setNames(rep(0L, length(coder_prefs)), names(coder_prefs))

  coder1 <- character(N)
  coder2 <- character(N)

  # pass 1: best match → lower load
  for (i in seq_len(N)) {
    s_sdgs <- df_group$sdg_set[[i]]
    c1 <- pick_best_coder(names(coder_prefs), s_sdgs, loads, coder_prefs)
    if (is.na(c1)) {
      # fallback to least loaded
      c1 <- names(sort(loads, decreasing = FALSE))[1]
    }
    coder1[i] <- c1
    loads[c1] <- loads[c1] + 1L
  }

  # pass 2: different coder, same rule
  for (i in seq_len(N)) {
    s_sdgs <- df_group$sdg_set[[i]]
    c1 <- coder1[i]
    c2 <- pick_best_coder(names(coder_prefs), s_sdgs, loads, coder_prefs, exclude = c1)
    if (is.na(c2)) {
      # fallback: least loaded not equal to c1
      least <- setdiff(names(sort(loads, decreasing = FALSE)), c1)
      c2 <- least[1]
    }
    coder2[i] <- c2
    loads[c2] <- loads[c2] + 1L
  }

  df_group %>% mutate(coder_1 = coder1, coder_2 = coder2)
}



# Run within each stratum to keep mixes balanced across strata
assigned_pairs <- stmts %>%
  mutate(.row_order = row_number()) %>%
  group_by(stratum) %>%
  arrange(.row_order, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  group_modify(~ assign_pref_double(.x, coder_sdgs)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-.row_order)
```

```{r - assign - diagnostics}
#   # arrange(desc(items)) %>%
#   arrange(coder_id)

# preference hit rates (how often a coder got at least one preferred SDG)
pref_hit <- assigned_pairs %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(coder_1, coder_2), names_to = "slot", values_to = "coder_id") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(hit = as.integer(any((sdg_set %||% integer(0)) %in% (coder_sdgs[[coder_id]] %||% integer(0))))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(coder_id) %>%
  summarise(pref_hits = sum(hit), total = n(), hit_rate = pref_hits / total) %>%
  arrange(desc(hit_rate)) %>%
  arrange(coder_id)

pref_hit

# ----------------------------
# Long format for downstream (salted dupes, exports, etc.)
# ----------------------------
assign_long <- assigned_pairs %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(coder_1, coder_2),
               names_to = "coder_slot", values_to = "coder_id") %>%
  mutate(is_duplicate = 0L,
         duplicate_group_id = NA_character_)

```




```{r - add salted duplicates}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Salted duplicates per coder
# ------------------------------------------------------------

duplicate_rate = 0.05

source(here('code', 'function_inject_duplicates.R'))

# Apply per coder
per_coder_queues <- assign_long %>%
  group_split(coder_id) %>%
  map_df(~ inject_duplicates(.x, dup_rate = duplicate_rate))

# Optional: ensure no accidental double-duplication within the same coder
# (Each coder should have at most 2 rows per statement: original + one duplicate)
per_coder_queues <- per_coder_queues %>%
  group_by(coder_id, statement_id) %>%
  mutate(dup_rank = row_number(desc(is_duplicate))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(dup_rank <= 2) %>%                # drop extras if any
  select(-dup_rank)



# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Diagnostics
# ------------------------------------------------------------
total_dupes <- sum(per_coder_queues$is_duplicate, na.rm = TRUE)
per_coder_dupes <- per_coder_queues %>%
  group_by(coder_id) %>%
  summarise(
    items_total   = n(),
    dupes         = sum(is_duplicate, na.rm = TRUE),
    originals     = items_total - dupes,
    dup_rate_real = ifelse(items_total > 0, dupes / originals, NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  # arrange(desc(dupes)) %>%
  arrange(coder_id)

cat(total_dupes, "total salted duplicates injected across all coders.\n")
print(per_coder_dupes)
```
